description: Per-volume coverage state, authored. The charter requires coverage reports to distinguish unknown, not-applicable, planned, partial, verified, inferred, deprecated, and superseded states; this file is where that judgment is recorded so it is reviewable in a diff. Page and heading metrics are measured by tools/build_volume_ledger.py and are not authored here.

states.unknown: The volume's coverage has not been assessed.
states.not-applicable: The volume does not apply to this knowledge base's scope.
states.planned: The subject is identified and named but not yet addressed. Pages may exist as stubs.
states.partial: The subject is addressed, with stated gaps. The default state for work in progress.
states.verified: Every load-bearing claim rests on observation of the thing described.
states.inferred: The material is sound but reasoned from documentation rather than observed. Distinct from partial: the gap is in evidence class, not in coverage extent.
states.superseded: Replaced by another volume; retained as a pointer.

1.rationale: Five pages carrying the L0/L1/L2 baseline. Cites no evidence record on any page, so the layer and domain models are asserted rather than sourced.

2.rationale: Eight boundary pages, scope narrowed deliberately by ADR 0001. The WMI-denial gap that made this volume documentation-only is closed: a 2026-07-30 observation recorded host edition, NTFS filesystem type, case-insensitivity, and a symlink-creation privilege requirement, and a 2026-07-31 observation closed the Registry, Security, and Networking rows. Console/ConPTY is the only row with no observation, and every finding is single-host, single-session.

3.rationale: Eleven pages, one per documented subsystem. Probes across three distinct MSYS runtimes cover process lifecycle, exec, signal delivery, fork emulation, symlink classification, and terminal-device presence, and show symlink behavior to be installation-dependent rather than a runtime constant. Path conversion, the mount table, and environment conversion still have no observation of any kind.

4.rationale: All six environments covered against the charter's eleven attributes. CLANGARM64 has no runtime observation at all - the observation host was x86_64 - so its behavioral sections are reasoned from CLANG64.

5.rationale: Thirty-one per-tool pages covering every family in the role model. Evidence is upstream documentation throughout; no tool page rests on a controlled run of the tool it describes.

6.rationale: The largest volume by an order of magnitude. Per-library pages plus seven category pages, now ranked on runtime and build-time edges alike. Two libraries — zlib and zstd (UCRT64) — carry full family classification from package-archive analysis; the rest are scoped to package and dependency evidence, because the deep-inventory pipeline has run against 2 of 15,711 packages.

7.rationale: Mechanism is grounded in Arch's pacman, pacman.conf, and alpm-hooks manual pages, and every page carries that caveat. A 2026-07-31 MSYS2 installation supplied real evidence for the transaction, hook, cache, and signature-validation rows, including pacman 6.1.0 itself. The tracked catalog snapshot predates that installation, so MSYS2's effective configuration for the snapshot this knowledge base composes remains uncaptured, and repair is unobserved.

8.rationale: Fifteen per-tool pages plus the LLVM umbrella. One bounded compile-and-execute probe and one completed zlib build exist; no toolchain binary has been analysed, and the llvm-tools file list is upstream's rather than observed.

9.rationale: Eight pages from gitforwindows.org and the Git manual pages, now anchored by controlled local observations: launcher hashes, a byte-level PE-import parse of git.exe, and three-shell-context PATH resolution. All of it is one workstation and one PATH configuration, and Git Credential Manager's repository was unreachable, so its internals are unverified.

10.rationale: Eight pages averaging fewer than two second-level headings each — the thinnest prose density in the knowledge base. The explorer itself is built and tested, and now carries a real D3 force-directed graph view; the volume documenting it is not written to the same standard, and the graph view has not been confirmed in a live browser.

11.rationale: The repository-to-package inventory is directly observed across 15,711 packages and 6 repositories, the strongest observational base in the knowledge base. The package-to-file inventory beneath it covers 2, with three further archive payloads analysed separately. docs/DEEP-INVENTORY-BLOCKER.md states what the remaining nine roadmap items wait on, which statements elsewhere are qualified by it, and the command that would close it.

12.rationale: Two pages. The provenance model and its collection boundary were already authored; what was missing was any measurement of the trees themselves. A 2026-08-03 pass added the measured shape from the recipe projection: 3,498 recipes across MSYS2-packages (458) and MINGW-packages (3,040) declaring 13,656 packages, 58% of recipes producing exactly four through ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX} expansion. Every figure is a floor, because the projection records a recipe only when one of its dependencies resolves. No claim ties a published archive to the recipe that names it; that needs source retrieval, patch application, and build evidence for one revision, which exists only for the bounded zlib slice.

13.rationale: One authored page over a substantial generated base: the reverse-dependency impact report exceeds a thousand lines and the dependency edges are observed. The analysis exists; the volume interpreting it does not.

14.rationale: Two pages. Recipes are ingested statically without executing PKGBUILDs, so build mechanics are modelled from declarations rather than from builds. MSYS2's effective makepkg.conf is uncaptured.

15.rationale: One page. Every extension point cites a concrete implementation except external plugin, where none exists. The compatibility mechanism is documented and has never been exercised in this repository's history.

16.rationale: One page carrying the threat model and supply-chain analysis. Cites no evidence record. The signing posture it would need to assess is the same one Volume 7 records as unestablished.

17.rationale: Contains no MSYS2 timings. Controlled observations exist on real MSYS2 installations, but none of them timed anything, so hot-path costs are derived from published algorithms; the pacman transaction shape is the one measured part.

18.rationale: Five pages answering select, build, debug, package, migrate, plus the repository workflow page. The repository workflow has been exercised end to end (PR #123); no command on the five MSYS2-facing pages has been executed, and each page says so.

19.rationale: Three pages covering upgrade, rollback, repair, migration, and refresh orchestration. Cites no evidence record; the procedures are authored rather than sourced or exercised.

20.rationale: Reference appendices including terminology, requirements traceability, this ledger, and the AKB tooling benchmarks re-filed here from Volume 17, whose two same-host samples live there. The only page in the knowledge base with a verified status sits in this volume.
